script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

JANE (mid 30s, earnest, wears glasses) is chopping vegetables while humming to herself. Suddenly, the front door bursts open. In walks MRS. JOAN (late 50s, stern, no-nonsense).

MRS. JOAN
(angry)
Jane! I can't believe you've done it again!

JANE
(surprised)
Done what, Mrs. Joan?

Mrs. Joan slams her purse on the kitchen counter.

MRS. JOAN
The flowers for the community garden! You've ruined them all!

JANE
(defensive)
I'm so sorry! I didn't mean to forget. I've been swamped with work.

Mrs. Joan rolls her eyes.

MRS. JOAN
(sighing)
It's always something with you, isn't it? I don't know how you manage to mess things up.

JANE
(apologetic)
I know I've made mistakes, Mrs. Joan. But I'm trying to do better. I truly am.

Mrs. Joan hesitates, then speaks softer.

MRS. JOAN
(grudgingly)
Fine. But you need to make it right. Go buy new flowers for the garden.

JANE
(nodding)
I will, Mrs. Joan. Thank you for giving me another chance.

INT. COMMUNITY GARDEN - DAY

Jane arrives at the garden with a bouquet of fresh flowers. She walks over to where Mrs. Joan is weeding.

JANE
(cheerfully)
Here are the new flowers, Mrs. Joan. I promise I won't forget again.

Mrs. Joan looks up at Jane, her expression softening.

MRS. JOAN
(smiling)
You're a good girl, Jane. I know you'll do better this time.

Jane beams, relieved.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jane sits at a table, sipping her coffee, when her phone buzzes with a text message. It's from MR. TOM (early 40s, kind, easygoing), the local florist.

TEXT MESSAGE: "Hi Jane, I'm sorry to bother you, but I have a question. Do you remember ordering a bouquet for Mrs. Joan last week?"

Jane feels a pang of guilt.

JANE
(texting)
Yes, I did. I'm so sorry I forgot to pay for it. Please hold the order and give me a minute to sort things out.

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

Jane explains the situation to Mrs. Joan, who is now seated at the kitchen table.

MRS. JOAN
(frustrated)
Why can't you keep track of things, Jane?

JANE
(apologetic)
I know, Mrs. Joan. I'm trying to be more responsible. But I made a mistake, and now I have to make things right.

Mrs. Joan sighs, then pulls out her wallet.

MRS. JOAN
Fine. You can pay me back.

JANE
(grateful)
Thank you, Mrs. Joan. I won't let you down again.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jane enters the coffee shop and approaches the counter, where Mr. Tom is waiting.

JANE
(embarrassed)
Hi, Mr. Tom. I'm so sorry for the mix-up with Mrs. Joan's flowers. I forgot to pay for them.

Mr. Tom smiles kindly.

MR. TOM
No need to be sorry, Jane. It happens to the best of us. But I appreciate your honesty and your determination to make things right.

Jane pays for the flowers and leaves the coffee shop, feeling a sense of relief and gratitude.

INT. COMMUNITY GARDEN - DAY

Jane arrives at the community garden with the fresh flowers for Mrs. Joan. She sees Mrs. Joan tending to the garden and approaches her.

JANE
(cheerfully)
Here are the new flowers for the garden, Mrs. Joan. I hope they make up for my mistake.

Mrs. Joan looks up and smiles.

MRS. JOAN
(forgiving)
You're forgiven, Jane. I know you're trying your best. And that's all I can ask for.

Jane beams, feeling a sense of closure and growth.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

Jane is cooking dinner when the doorbell rings. She opens the door to find MR. TOM, holding a bouquet of flowers.

MR. TOM
(smiling)
I thought you might like some fresh flowers for your kitchen table, Jane. No charge.

JANE
(grateful)
Thank you, Mr. Tom. That's very kind of you.

Mr. Tom waves it off.

MR. TOM
It's the least I can do for someone who's trying to make things right.

Jane smiles, touched by his kindness.

JANE
You're a good man, Mr. Tom.

Mr. Tom laughs.

MR. TOM
And you, Jane, are a good learner.

FADE OUT.

End screenplay.
